styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's visible tones per tile (8) are on par with the paving reference (7) and above the grass reference (3). Its dark edge pixels are mostly tinted (only 14% neutral), so the outline is a dark brown material tone rather than a black sticker line. The weaknesses are structural. The sand strip along the bottom is a broad, nearly flat fill, which explains the 21% near-flat coverage, whereas both references have 0%. The wooden step risers and posts are built from only about 3-4 lightness steps with little grain or per-plank variation. Across the whole patch there are only 11 distinct colours. Beside the references, with their per-stone and per-tuft shading, it reads flatter and more repetitive. Since this is a close call, it fails.

At 8 visible tones per tile it matches or beats the grass (3) and paving (7) references on density. However, the whole piece uses only 11 distinct colours, so each material ramp has about 4 steps (tread light, mid, dark gap, deep) against the references' 5-6.
